content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, it is critical to call 911 immediately. For other cases of overdose, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Laxatives should only be used temporarily and only when necessary to relieve constipation. Prolonged or frequent use of laxatives can result in chronic constipation and dependency on these medications. Refer to the How to Use section for further guidance. For proper storage, follow the instructions provided on the product's packaging. If you have any questions about storage, consult your pharmacist. Keep the product away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Medications should not be flushed down the toilet or poured into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health needs. Before using bisacodyl, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you have experienced a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks or require the use of a laxative for more than one week, consult your doctor before using this product. This medication may be used during labor and delivery to cleanse the bowels before the second stage of labor (pushing phase). At other times during pregnancy, it should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed on this medication and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laxatives should only be used temporarily for constipation relief. High doses or frequent use can lead to persistent constipation and dependency on laxatives. Refer to the How to Use section for additional details. For storage, follow the instructions on the package label. If you have questions about storage, consult your pharmacist. Protect the product from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
